correctness.rationale: For \(n\ge4\), preserving wheel rim distance is exactly preserving cycle adjacency, hence each proper domain induces \(r\) disjoint paths. For a path multiset with multiplicities \(m_j\), cyclic start/gap enumeration gives \(n(r-1)!\binom{n-k-1}{r-1}/\prod_jm_j!\) subsets. An ordered subset pair has \((\prod_jm_j!)2^{\sum_{j\ge2}m_j}\) isomorphisms. Their product summed via the weighted generating function \(u(x)=x(1+x)/(1-x)\) yields the exact coefficient formula. Rank zero is the empty map and full-rim automorphisms form a dihedral group of order \(2n\). For \(s=\lfloor n/2\rfloor\), \(s!\le T_n\le4^n2^s s!+2n\), hence \(\log T_n/(n\log n)\to1/2\). The number \(E_n\) of extendible elements lies between \(2n\) and \(2n2^n\); therefore \(\log(E_n/T_n)/(n\log n)\to-1/2\). Independently enumerated actual maps verify all rank counts through \(n=7\); subset-signature and exact-coefficient verifications cover \(3\le n\le12\). All computations are finite corroboration only.

value.rationale: Exact cardinality by element-domain rank is a basic invariant of the specifically studied inverse monoid and is not the previously determined generator-set rank. The complete formula and provable half-factorial entropy distinguish the wheel metric from intrinsic cycle distance. The quantified superexponential rarity of extendible maps is a meaningful structural boundary revealing most partial symmetries cannot arise from ambient automorphisms, beyond a routine small-case enumeration.
